reviews.text:
Maki Nori is dangerous… because once you eat here, every other sushi place tastes like supermarket sadness. 🍣😂

The sushi was so fresh I’m pretty sure the salmon made eye contact with me. The rolls were packed, perfectly made, and disappeared from the plate faster than my paycheck on payday.

Service was amazing too — a huge shoutout to Lincoln, Kaitlin, and Kayleigh for making the experience even better. They were friendly, attentive, quick with everything, and somehow managed to keep smiling even when I ordered “just one more roll” five different times. They made us feel genuinely welcome from start to finish.

Honestly, if happiness had a flavor, it would probably be the spicy tuna from Maki Nori. Between the incredible food and the outstanding service from Lincoln, Kaitlin, and Kayleigh, this place is an easy recommendation.

Highly recommend — unless you enjoy boring food and disappointment.

reviews.author: Lesley Harding
reviews.text:
Disappointing.
The food is simple and of similar quality to popular takeaway sushi chains. The fish was not of the quality promised. Rice was not seasoned and despite advertising fresh wasabi online this was at an additional cost. Dry ice used on the omakase set felt gimmicky and unnecessary. Gyoza were oily and tasted frozen. Sea bream crudo was incredibly sweet. Cheese tart was overcooked, not enjoyable and came very late.

Staff did not seem informed about the food - for example they were not to able to explain to us what fish was being used for the day for the omakase set.

Our waiter, however, did try very hard to make up for the shortcomings of the restaurant and we could see he was doing his very best to be as helpful as possible.

The restaurant itself was also surprisingly worn despite having opened fairly recently. Table did not look clean and seating very tightly spaced  around it so not very comfortable for 4 adults. Additionally, we were not given anything to clean our hands with prior to being served the handrolls directly by the chef.

Having eaten at many other Japanese restaurants in London and Japan this did not represent the best Japanese food London has to offer which was a shame.

reviews.author: Kom Kantha
reviews.text:
I had an amazing experience at Maki Nori!!!

The food was outstanding, and the fish was incredibly fresh. Every dish was prepared beautifully and tasted delicious. You can really tell that they care about the quality of their ingredients.

What impressed me most was the service. The staff were proactive, attentive, and genuinely cared about their customers. There was a small mistake with one of our orders, as it was accidentally served to the wrong table, which caused a bit of a delay. They apologised and generously gave us four complimentary maki rolls as well as the mistaken order for free. It was a very thoughtful gesture and showed how much they value customer satisfaction.

A special mention to the chef, who was incredibly kind, friendly, and welcoming throughout our visit. Their positive attitude made the experience even more memorable.

LOVE ITTT

reviews.author: Imjustforeign
reviews.text:
I’d happily give more than 5 stars if I could.

Sarah was genuinely one of the best waitresses I’ve ever had, and that’s coming from someone who has travelled quite a bit and eaten in restaurants all over the world. From the moment we sat down, she brought an incredible amount of energy, positivity, and enthusiasm that completely transformed the experience.

Her smile was infectious, her personality was so bubbly and cheerful, and she made every interaction feel natural and fun. She wasn’t just serving food—she was creating an experience. The service was flawless from start to finish, and she made sure we were looked after throughout the entire visit.

One of my favourite moments was when she let me do the drum and even taught me a little Japanese, which made the visit even more memorable. It’s those little personal touches that people remember long after they’ve left the restaurant.

A big thank you as well to the manager, whose name I unfortunately forgot to ask for. We had a lovely chat, and he told me Sarah is always like this. I was genuinely shocked when he mentioned that even on her bad days she’s still the same positive, energetic person. That’s something I really admire. She doesn’t let a bad day affect how she treats other people, which honestly she reminded me a lot of SpongeBob 😂.

All jokes aside, Sarah is an absolute credit to Maki & Ramen. She brings so much joy, energy, and positivity to the restaurant, and it’s rare to meet someone who clearly loves making other people smile.

If I could give 20 out of 5 stars, I would.

Thank you, Sarah, for making our visit unforgettable. You’re an absolute star. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (20/5 if Google would let me!) 😄
complaint_clauses: unfortunately forgot to ask for.

Went here and was simply blown away by the food, the hospitality and the atmosphere.

We were met with a very lovely woman when we arrived (I think she said her name was Daytona? Sorry if I am butchering that spelling!) Who couldn't do wnough for us. She very clearly enjoyed her job and it reflected in her enthusiasm.

We were then met by several other waiters, each of whom were lovely but the standout has to be Ginje (again apologies on butchering the name) who was such a character!

The food was absolutely divine and is the ONLY place we have ever asked to see the menu again, the drinks were also inventive and fun.

The atmosphere itself was fun, bright colours, a feeling of being in a bubble of Tokyo away from the bustling streets of London and a great respite away from the heat above on the streets.

Thoroughly recommend anyone visits whilst in London.

Only caveat would be to the owner putting wifi boostees down in the basement so the poor waiters aren't having to dance about for signal on their card readers!

I recently visited Maki & Ramen and had a good experience overall. The ambiance is nice and comfortable. Paid parking is available on the surrounding streets, which was convenient.

The food was tasty, and I ordered the Steak Ramen, which I really enjoyed. One thing I appreciated is that they offer halal options. The halal items are clearly marked on the menu, and the staff also confirm this when taking your order. Even so, I would still recommend mentioning that you want the halal option when ordering, just to be certain.

Overall, the food was flavorful, the staff were helpful, and I’d be happy to visit again.

reviews.text: A friend and I came across Maki Nori back when it was newly opened, when we were looking for a place to have a light bite and we were convinced to try their menu from taste testing their temaki rolls when they were just promoting the restaurant. My first impressions is that the staff are very friendly from the manager whom we had a general conversation to the waiter who not only explained the menu to the best of his ability, as the place was very new at the time but also had a conversation as well. We ordered pork gyozas and traditional Japanese chicken karaage, which was crispy & tasty and our main bites was the 8 piece omakase which I generally enjoyed trying each and every individual piece made by the sushi chef, who also explained to us where the fish were caught and came from. Generally omakase can be expensive so as an taster of omakase is Maki Nori is a great place to try especially as it isn't very expensive. This place is a great place to have that sushi, omakase experience or share some light bites at decent prices.

reviews.author: CY
reviews.text:
I recently visited Maki & Nori in Central London with my parents, and unfortunately the experience did not justify the price.

The service was disappointing from the start. Despite the restaurant being nearly empty, empty plates were rarely cleared from our table. We eventually had to stack them ourselves to make room, yet staff would often remove only one plate and leave the rest behind.

The restaurant’s signature hand roll trolley is an interesting concept, but the experience felt rushed rather than enjoyable. I ordered 2 of the A5 Wagyu hand roll (£15 each), and the server accidentally dropped part of the wagyu during each preparation without apologising or replacing it. After every bite, we were repeatedly asked for feedback and comparisons before we had even finished eating, which made it difficult to simply enjoy the food.

The tuna hand roll was decent, but overall the food was average. The wagyu in both the hand roll and nigiri was surprisingly chewy, and portion sizes were noticeably smaller than most sushi restaurants in London. I was also concerned to see containers of raw tuna sitting open on the hand roll trolley.

We spent £288 for three people. For the price, the food quality, portion sizes and service simply did not deliver.

If you’re looking for authentic, high-quality Japanese food, I don’t think Maki & Nori is worth the cost. The restaurant focuses heavily on the hand roll experience, but the food itself and overall dining experience fell well below expectations.

(Translated by Google) While there's a wide variety of ramen, the noodles don't blend well with the soup, resulting in a lack of excitement. The soup itself is unique and delicious, but the noodles overpower the flavor, which is a shame.

The Hell Ramen, with its spicy pork bone broth, was tasty. Therefore, I felt it was a pity that if the noodles were of higher quality, it would be worth the price, or even more.

They seem to beat a drum every time a customer enters, and because the restaurant is large, the sound echoes, which I personally found noisy. Other customers were startled and looked towards the entrance each time the drum sounded. Since there's no culture of beating drums in Japanese restaurants (it's more common at festivals or perhaps in izakayas?), it left a strange impression.

reviews.text:
The Anti-Hype Review ⭐⭐**
Everyone’s hyping GDK and I hate hype. So I went with zero expectations. Here’s the truth: It’s not magic. It’s just… well-executed. Bread is crispy because they actually toast it. Meat is good because they don’t overcook it. Sauce is light because German doner isn’t supposed to be a mayo bomb. They give extra if you ask, which most places act like you’re insulting them for asking. Metrocenter food court has 20 food stalls, but most taste the same after 3 bites. This one doesn’t. Is it worth the price? If you care about proper doner, yes. If you just want “full pet”, go eat rice. But for actual kebab? Uncommonly good.

reviews.text:
Update: After I left this review, the management contacted me to apologise for the experience and invited me back. They were courteous, professional, and clearly took the feedback seriously.

I have since returned and had a much better experience. The food was back to the standard I've come to expect from Maki Ramen, which is why I've updated my rating.

My original takeaway experience was still disappointing, but I appreciate the way the restaurant handled the situation and their commitment to customer service.

----------------------------

I have eaten at Maki Ramen many times, both at this location and at their other restaurants, and the food is usually of a good standard. Unfortunately, this takeaway order was extremely disappointing.

We ordered the Tiger Roll and Rainbow Roll, and the quality of the sushi was far below what we have come to expect. The sushi rice was so wet and overworked that you could barely see the individual grains. It had a slimy texture and completely ruined the eating experience. As soon as you picked up a piece of sushi, all of the ingredients fell out because it had not been assembled properly.

It felt as though no care or attention had been taken when preparing the order. To make matters worse, no wasabi, ginger, chopsticks, or serviettes were included with the takeaway.

This was a very poor experience and not at all reflective of the quality we have previously enjoyed from Maki Ramen. I hope this was a one-off issue, but it was disappointing enough that I felt compelled to leave a review.

reviews.text:
We have visited Maki & Ramen five times now, and unfortunately the level of service has been very inconsistent. Our visit yesterday was by far the worst and has left us deciding not to return.

We were a family of five, and I joined the group shortly after finishing work. We asked if we could move from our table to an available booth as it offered more space for our party. We were told this was not possible because our food order had already been assigned to the table and we would need to wait until all the food had arrived before moving. This made little sense to us as the booth was directly next to our table.

What made the situation more frustrating was that the booth was later given to a group of three, while our party of five had to squeeze around two small tables with dishes balanced across them. With a bill of around £120, I would expect a better level of customer service and a little more flexibility where possible.

In addition, the member of staff we spoke to had a very noticeable body odour, which was unfortunately apparent whenever food was brought to the table. I appreciate this may be an uncomfortable issue to raise, but when customers are dining, hygiene and presentation are important parts of the experience.

Throughout the meal, no one checked whether we were okay despite the obvious lack of space, and no effort was made to revisit the request or offer any alternative solution. After visiting several times previously, it is disappointing that our final experience was so poor.

The food itself was enjoyable, but the service and overall experience left a very negative impression. Sadly, after five visits, we will not be returning.

reviews.text:
We visited this Maki & Ramen location twice, and over both visits, the food was exceptional. The Black Dragon roll and Black Garlic Tonkotsu are standout entries on the menu, and we couldn't recommend the food here enough.

However, on a fairly busy Saturday evening visit, I was left for approx. 30 mins without food while my husband was served his very promptly. In fairness, our waitress did explain that what I had ordered was taking an "extra 15 minutes", but after those 15 minutes had been and gone, and it had actually turned into 30 minutes, all I could do during that time was watch him eat his order by himself before it went cold.... and I just got hungrier.

When my food did eventually arrive, it was as I said exceptional, but now it was a role reversal, and I was the one left eating by myself instead.

The music was also quite loud, and it was impossible to have a normal conversation without shouting at eachother.

On balance I'd definitely recommend this location, but if Saturday's service is anything to go by, don't arrive hungry and ready to eat, because you'll be "hangry" by the time your food gets to you.

reviews.text:
Came across Maki Nori as I was wandering Soho and dropped in for a solo dinner. I sat at the bar and it was a lot of fun to watch the chefs work. The service from the entire staff was incredible, Gabriel and Luca were super attentive and offered suggestions.

I ordered the 6 piece omakase, the chef's ceviche and the spicy tuna roll. The omakase was SO beautiful and delicious. Each one that they sent out was slightly different, showing that it really is just "what the chef feels like", which made it feel so personal. I've had Omakase where it's the same menu all night which is fine but I ordered this. It was very cool watching him prepare each one.

The chef's ceviche was also next level, I would eat that every single day.

I don't usually find spicy tuna rolls to be that hot, but this one lived up to its name and was very spicy.

I finished off with the Hokkaido cheese tart which was warm and light, a nice way to end the meal

Overall, very good experience. I will definitely be back!

reviews.author: ランチウェイ
reviews.text:
(Translated by Google) I ordered black garlic tonkotsu ramen, edamame, and Sapporo beer at Maki Ramen in Glasgow. Overall, the black garlic tonkotsu ramen exceeded my expectations; the soup had a rich flavor, and I enjoyed the aroma of black garlic. On the other hand, the char siu was just average, and a little on the salty side. The noodles were also slightly different from the noodles you'd find in authentic ramen in Japan, and perhaps they were cooked for a little too short a time. However, this is Glasgow, not Japan. Considering that, I feel like I can't expect anything more. Overall, I'd give the taste about 75 points, and I think it's a perfectly enjoyable place to eat ramen in Glasgow. The edamame was served warm. This is a common style in Europe, so I didn't mind it too much. It paired well with the Sapporo beer. The service was quick, and the staff were friendly. Most of the waitstaff seemed to be local Scots, but the person in charge of sushi appeared to be Japanese or of Asian descent. Overall, it's a place where you can easily enjoy ramen and Japanese food in Glasgow.

reviews.text: I want to preface my review of this restaurant by giving a mention to the two very welcoming staff members who were the reason my friend and I made the visit to Maki Nori. The staff were great, I can’t fault the service and the atmosphere inside was warm and provides a space that a real omakase restaurant does but I can’t help but feel there was a bit of false advertisement going on. The food was nothing special. My friend and I got the 15 piece ‘omakase’ but it came all on one plate? The quality of fish was so average and borderline not fresh, but it might have been different for the more expensive cuts of fish like the Chutoro tuna that I saw other people order. The fish that featured on the ‘omakase’ set was average at best - we were really surprised when it arrived. The lemon zest on the salmon nigiri added nothing and seemed like an attempt to fancify a simple item that needed no embellishment had the fish quality been at a certain standard. To provide a comparison, Eat Tokyo’s quality of fish is much better and sits at a better price range but I guess the atmosphere is something new…

Ground floor seating was a bit uncomfortable, quite a few tables close together so somewhat noisy and you feel a bit like you're in a corridor especially if your back is facing the area people are walking through. We got the lunch deal which was very reasonably priced and promised to arrive in under thirty minutes (good if you're in a rush). It did arrive quite promptly.
For the speed and price I think you get what you'd expect for the food. It's about average in most places though the vegan chicken used in the Vegan Chicken Katsu was notably a bit cardboardy.
Come for quick, reliable, and reasonably priced food but don't expect it to rival the quality of food from independent Japanese restaurants in the area.

reviews.author: Mamnoon
reviews.text: Came here because of all the glowing reviews. Just finished my food and I feel immense disappointment. I got the beef steak ramen (the halal version) and my friend got the miso chicken ramen. The broth was an embarrassment. In fact if you told me that it was water with some salt and soy sauce added I would have believed it. The meat portion was small, but the overall dish did leave me feeling full. But the overall lack of any depth or taste in the broth took away from any possible satisfaction that the fullness could've given me. I also got takoyaki which in all fairness was decent. Also having to use the QR code over and over again to order refills for our water is a bit dark in my humble opinion. The only thing positive about the place is how quick they got the food to us and the pretty location and seating. So if you're here for the aesthetics this is the place for you. But if you're here expecting decent food please don't bother. The pictures are decieving.

But my goodness it was so flavourful and fulling. To top it off, the customer service was amazing. There was a little bit of a wait but I wasn’t shocked with how popular it is. I loved how they hit the barrel every time a customer was seated, I’ve never seen anywhere do something like that. Definitely a new favourite for whenever I’m in town.

The Matcha Scam: I ordered a matcha latte based on the beautiful, vibrant green pictures in the menu (as seen in image). What I actually received was a muddy brown drink with zero hint of green. Charging 6.5 for total false advertising is a scam.

The Awful Tempura: The food was just as disappointing. The tempura was incredibly greasy, soggy, and coated in a ridiculously thick layer of batter. Real tempura is supposed to be light and crispy, but this felt like thick flour dough dropped in oil. One bite and my mouth was literally pooling with grease.

We really enjoyed the food at Maki & Ramen Leeds. The sushi was fresh and full of flavour, while the ramen was rich, comforting, and clearly made with quality ingredients. The prices were also very reasonable for the standard of the food.

Gaby, who served our table, was incredibly friendly, attentive, and efficient throughout our visit. She gave us some excellent recommendations, and we were glad we took her advice because everything we tried was delicious. The mocktails were refreshing and complemented the meal perfectly.

For dessert, the mochi and matcha brownie were absolutely fantastic and were the perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, we had a wonderful dining experience. Huge thanks to Gaby and the team, we’ll definitely be coming back again soon!

I thought I’d be safe with the ramen option and my friend ordered a rack of sushi. The food came pretty quickly despite the slow service .
The sushi was cut so thick and messy with what looked like the ending or trimming of left over fish on the top like they ran out of ingredients ? The ramen I ordered came luke warm, noodles were undercooked but stuck together and only had two king prawns and two thin slices of salmon inside.

The service was also so so slow. There was only 1 person who seemed to be taking everyone’s orders bless her and she looked understandably stressed. The lady rolling the sushi’s looked like she couldn’t really be bothered and it showed from how the rolls came out :(

The only good thing was the Japanese fizzy drink the waitress recommended and catching up with my friend but now regretting it all as I vomit

Sadly won’t be returning again.

reviews.author: Hemaxi
reviews.text:
Never going back. First and last visit.

We arrived slightly earlier for our table for 2 booked for 7pm and were seated, no problem. We were waiting around 15 minutes for our drinks order to be taken, and we chose to order food at the same time.

Drinks came over with a very confused server. To us, it was clear the drinks were for us and the table next to us judging by the number of glasses and people. She had to go away and check and then come back to finally give us the drinks.

After that, my food arrived first and we had to wait another 10 minutes or so before my friend's food arrived. My food was getting cold by then. But they served the meat option when the vegan option had been ordered. They took it away and came back another 15 minutes or so later with the correct meal. They didn't even apologise.

The bill came with service charge included and in my opinion, they should have taken the initiative to take money off considering they served meat to someone who doesn't even eat meat. I requested they reconsider, and they returned with another bill with a drink and service charge removed. Ridiculous that we had to ask for that in the first place considering the poor service, but grateful they did do something about the bill. It was at this point we finally had an apology.

reviews.author: Zhen Liu
reviews.text: Rather disappointing experience. We were seated in the middle of everyone and asked if we could move to a booth and this was granted by the waiter. Then what appeared to be the maitre d' came over and told us that we cannot sit there because it was for 4 people and was shoved into a corner of the restaurant. Not a great start, staff should be clear on that. Anyway ordered the salmon sushi platter with sashimi, nigiri and uramaki rolls. The sashimi was far from fresh. You can see in the pictures where the flesh is tearing and just falling apart from being picked up. Not good enough at all. The avocado was rock hard and clearly not ripe in the uramaki. Also no bowl for the soy sauce (edit: I had to use the bowl that the extra egg was served in) . You're expected to drown your sushi in the plate it's served on. We ordered the clam sashimi too but the nigiri version arrived instead. We were told we could have the nigiri on the house which is a nice touch but it's only two measley pieces anyway. The one good thing was the ramen itself. Ordered the original tonkotsu and the black garlic version. Both were really good, broth was excellent as were the egg and pork. Just a little bit silly to serve in such an enormous bowl, it looked ridiculous and unnecessary especially when the tables were so incredibly small. It's no better than the other big chains like ippudo so I wouldn't go out of my way for the ramen. If you're lucky you might also get the maitre d' teaching you to pour your broth over your ramen pork to infuse the flavour as if you were a child. Just what customers want. Lastly the food just comes out whenever it's ready which is fine but I'd expect both ramens to come out at the same time...it's not like adding some garlic sauce makes it delayed 5 minutes thereby forcing one person to wait to eat and leaving their food to go cold. Complete amateurs and it's incredible this place has 4.9 stars. It goes to show how little standards we hold for eating out these days.

reviews.author: Richard
reviews.text:
🥩Seared Beef Tataki
The beef is cooked to medium perfection, and the noodles have a wonderful springy texture. This spicy chili oil doesn’t hit you with extreme heat, but the aroma is incredibly rich and flavorful.

🦐Dynamite Prawns
Crispy fried prawns paired with a rich, flavorful sauce — each bite is such a satisfying treat. Pair them with a cold beer or one of the house cocktails, and you’ve got yourself a truly great meal.

🍣Grilled Sushi
• Eel: The smoky, charred flavor from grilling makes the eel taste even more intense and delicious.
• Prawn: Grilling locks in the natural sweetness of the prawns, adding deeper layers of flavor to every bite.
• Scallop: Scallops are already naturally sweet and tender, and grilling amplifies that sweetness beautifully.

🐟Three Kinds of Sashimi + Octopus + Sea Bream
Great value for money! The sashimi is cut thick, portions are generous, and everything is incredibly fresh — the quality is far better than you’d expect from a restaurant at this price point.

🍣Salmon & Avocado Sushi Tube
Such a clever and stylish design! The soy sauce is stored in a thin tube, and you can squeeze out just the right amount to push onto the sushi one piece at a time. You can also add soy sauce little by little whenever you like, so you never use more than you need.
complaint_clauses: but the aroma is incredibly rich and flavorful.
Pair them with a cold beer or one of the house cocktails, and you’ve got yourself a truly great meal.
You can also add soy sauce little by little whenever you like, so you never use more than you need.

reviews.text: We arrived at the restaurant as a group of three diners for dinner at 9:00 PM. Although we had reserved seats in advance, it took about five minutes to get us into the restaurant, during which we waited at the entrance until the hostess, who was also a waitress, would clear up. After we sat down, we ordered drinks and food together, the waiter took our order and returned a few minutes later to inform us that the drink we requested was out of stock, and then again a few minutes later to inform us that we actually had some. We ordered some rolls that were incredibly delicious, the crispiness of the seaweed was exceptional, and overall we really enjoyed the quality of the food. Unfortunately, we were mainly disappointed with the service - we were not contacted during the meal, and around 10:00 PM we wanted to order additional dishes, but the waiter informed us that the chef had already closed the kitchen a few minutes ago. It is unclear why diners do not receive an update beforehand, especially since there were other diners in the restaurant who were still eating. Regarding the cleanliness of the place, it is mediocre.

reviews.author: J M
reviews.text:
(Translated by Google) Maki & Ramen (located near Chinatown) has a really convenient location; it's just a few minutes' walk from Leicester Square, Soho, and Chinatown. It's open quite late, making it perfect for late-night diners.

The interior has a dark, slightly cyberpunk feel, with neon lights and a huge Tokyo projection screen, creating a great photo opportunity. It's a great atmosphere for gatherings with friends or dates.

🥢Tonkotsu Ramen: The broth is quite rich, with a strong pork bone flavor, but not overly greasy. Those who like rich broth ramen will likely enjoy it. The chashu is seared, making it even more fragrant. Overall, it's a solid choice and hard to go wrong with.

🥩Beef Ramen: The beef steak is cooked to perfection, not dry at all. The slightly spicy broth is surprisingly refreshing and adds more depth than expected. If it's your first time and you're unsure what to order, I'd recommend this one.

🦞Seafood Ramen
The seafood selection was quite generous, including shrimp, salmon, and squid. The broth was a bit lighter than tonkotsu, but still very flavorful, perfect for summer or for those who don't like overly heavy broths.

Overall, the three bowls of ramen were quite generous in portion size. Two bowls plus a few side dishes would be more than enough for two people.

🍗The side dishes were a pleasant surprise.
Both the teriyaki fried chicken and sweet and sour fried chicken (Sweet Chilli) are worth ordering.
The outer skin was crispy, while the chicken inside was still very juicy. The two sauces each had their own unique characteristics: one was sweet and fragrant, the other had a slightly sweet, sour, and spicy flavor. I personally preferred the sweet and sour fried chicken; it was so delicious I couldn't stop eating it.

🐙Takoyaki
It was as expected, with a slightly crispy outer layer and a soft interior. It was delicious when hot and went perfectly with the ramen.

🍰Save room for dessert!
The matcha cake with vanilla ice cream was surprisingly good.

The matcha wasn't too bitter, the cake was moist, and the ice cream perfectly balanced the sweetness. It was a refreshing treat after a meal.

🍸 Drink Recommendations
We ordered two cocktails that day.

🤍 Fuji Mountain (the white one): The creamy and liqueur flavors were well-balanced, and it looked beautiful.

💙 The blue one, which I immediately nicknamed Tokyo Blue 😂, was a really photogenic color—a refreshing type, perfect for summer.

Their cocktails are generally delicious and photogenic.

💰 Overall Summary

✔️ Photogenic ambiance

✔️ Rich ramen broth

✔️ Surprisingly good snacks

✔️ Definitely worth trying the cocktails

✔️ Average price per person: £25–30

Maki & Ramen（中国城附近这家）位置真的很方便，Leicester Square、Soho、中国城一路逛过来几分钟就到，晚上营业时间也比较晚，夜宵党很友好。

店里整体偏暗色调，有一点赛博朋克的感觉，霓虹灯加上超大的 Tokyo 投影，拍照特别出片，朋友聚餐或者约会氛围都不错。

🥢豚骨拉面
汤底属于比较浓郁的类型，猪骨香味很足，但不会特别腻，喜欢浓汤拉面的应该都会喜欢。叉烧炙烤过之后香气更明显，整体比较稳，不容易踩雷。

🥩牛排拉面
牛排熟度控制得不错，口感不会柴，搭配带一点辣味的汤底反而很解腻，比想象中更有层次。如果第一次来不知道点什么，我会比较推荐这一款。

🦞海鲜拉面
海鲜给得挺有诚意，虾、三文鱼、鱿鱼都有，汤底比豚骨清爽一点，但鲜味还是在线，很适合夏天或者不喜欢特别厚重汤底的人。

整体来说三碗拉面的分量都不小，两个人点两碗再配几份小食其实就已经很够吃。

🍗 小食反而给了我惊喜
照烧炸鸡和糖醋炸鸡（Sweet Chilli）都值得点。
外皮炸得很酥，里面鸡肉还是很多汁，两种酱汁各有特色，一个偏甜香，一个带一点酸甜微辣，我个人更喜欢糖醋炸鸡，真的会忍不住一直吃。

🐙 章鱼小丸子
属于正常发挥，外皮微脆，里面软软的，热的时候很好吃，配拉面刚刚好。

🍰 甜品一定要留肚子
抹茶蛋糕配香草冰淇淋意外不错。
抹茶不会特别苦，蛋糕湿润度也可以，加上冰淇淋一起吃刚好中和甜度，吃完整餐以后来一份很舒服。

🍸 饮品推荐
当天点了两杯鸡尾酒。
🤍 Fuji Mountain（富士山） 是白色那杯，奶香和酒感比较平衡，颜值也很高。
💙 蓝色那杯我直接给它起名 Tokyo Blue 😂，颜色真的很适合拍照，清爽类型，很适合夏天。
他们家的鸡尾酒整体都属于好喝又出片系列。

💰 整体总结
✔️ 环境很出片
✔️ 拉面汤底偏浓郁
✔️ 小吃比预期更惊喜
✔️ 鸡尾酒值得点
✔️ 人均约 £25–30

The other day, I had such a wonderful experience at Maki Ramen! We arrived very close to closing time, and I honestly expected to be turned away, but Ginger was so welcoming and kindly let us come in. Even though the staff were busy getting ready to close, he remained friendly, patient, and provided excellent service the entire time.

Our server, IMI, was absolutely amazing. He was so kind, attentive, and genuinely caring. He checked in to make sure everything was okay, and every request we had was met with a smile, even while the team was busy closing for the night. His positive attitude and willingness to help made our dining experience so enjoyable.

Ginger and IMI are exactly the kind of people who make a restaurant memorable. Their kindness, professionalism, and dedication to great customer service are rare, and they truly deserve recognition. These are the kinds of people we need more of in the service industry. Thank you both for making our visit such a great experience, I can't wait to come back!
- S

reviews.text:
★★★☆☆ 3/5 — Great drinks, so-so mains

Went here for dinner with my wife, friend and his misses  — a lively spot with a good soundtrack (props for the Feel Good Inc and Promiscuous throwback) and a fun greeting on arrival with a big drum bong. Good energy from the start.

The cocktails genuinely stole the show. My wife's rose cocktail came out in a rose-shaped glass with a smoky liquid nitrogen effect — properly impressive presentation. The Hanami was more understated but the flavour more than made up for the simpler glass. Easily 10/10 on drinks.

The sushi held up its end too — fresh, bright, well-made rolls with nothing to fault (8.5/10).

The kitchen was the weak link, though. The chashu yakisoba had well-cooked, al dente noodles, but the sauce leaned sweet with little else going on. The Steak Tataki Ramen was the bigger letdown — the beef was bland and the broth underwhelming, especially at that price point. The chashu pork itself was genuinely great, just surrounded by dishes that didn't back it up.

Service was attentive and friendly throughout (8/10).

Overall: come for the drinks and sushi, don't expect much from the ramen. £82 for two felt steep given the food didn't match the price.

the broth underwhelming

reviews.summary: Bland steak tataki ramen and broth, sweet yakisoba sauce, steep for food quality

She guided us through the menu with great recommendations, answered all our questions, and checked on us throughout the meal to make sure everything was perfect. If you’re in the area, do yourself a favor and stop by. This place is going to be a neighborhood favorite and we’ll definitely be back soon. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Damian Lubanski
reviews.text:
First of all congrats to entire team with opening another site and busy launch.

Ren's attention and understanding of my sarcasm left me with more that positive feeling. I'd say entire team was doing their best from from what I could gather, even when big groups of customers - seven or more - would like to split the bill - if that's what friendship/trust means in 2026, please sign me off. I was even asked by three different people if everything's all right in quick succession, which is a bit too much for me, but I get it: it's new team, people learn how to work with each other, I already know they've got a great team there. Ren deserves a pay rise though, his suggestion about Steak tataki was spot on, even it was my choice anyway.

Ramen was very good, not the best I've ever had but with so many places in London, bar is set very high. I'd say this ramen lacks some deeper flavours and there is not much aftertaste when meal is done.

Blueberry matcha was excellent though, the best blueberry matcha I've had; I'd say it's elevated matcha because ice is crushed so tinnily that glass looks like a small ice lake, cool effect and sounds more interesting than usual ice cubes.

Atmosphere and décor was great too, they even have a garden which is a welcoming addition and with cherry blossom effect inside and open kitchen and bar, this site appears more like a premium place. Good choice of music.

Highly recommend for service and atmosphere.

All the best.

A great place in Edinburgh for some ramen and sushi. We were a party of four and ordered a variety of dishes including a couple of starters.

We also ordered a rainbow sushi roll that was outstanding!
The portions were very generous and we thought about ordering some matcha ice cream balls for dessert but we just didn't have any room left.
They do a very healthy take away business as there was a consistent flow of "To Go" orders heading out the door
We arrived early and were sitted straight away. I would recommend a reservation if you are planning to eat later in the evening, as the restaurant filled up by 18:00 on a Friday evening.

I visited Maki & Ramen Southampton today and I am genuinely speechless.

🎉This is the only restaurant in Southampton that truly cares about coeliac and gluten‑free customers, and they proved it from the moment I ordered.

🎉I asked for ramen made completely gluten‑free — something most places either refuse or charge extra for — and they prepared it without any fuss, without any hesitation, and without charging a single extra penny.

The care, the kindness, and the confidence they showed made the whole experience feel effortless.The food was delicious🍜🍛🍚🍘🍥🍙🍱, the service was warm, and the team were an absolutely lovely bunch of people.

You’ve earned a solid 5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ from me, and I will definitely be coming back. Thank you for making dining out safe, easy, and joyful for gluten‑free customers.

Thank you Mia and the Team!

reviews.author: Hon Arroyo
reviews.text:
Looking for the best ramen and sushi in Southampton? Look no further than Maki & Ramen, located on Level 4 of Westquay. This spot is quickly becoming a local favorite, delivering an authentic taste of Tokyo right to Hampshire.
Here is why it is earned a flawless 5-star vibe:
8-Hour Slow-Cooked Broth: Their signature Tonkotsu Ramen features a rich, velvety pork bone broth simmered for eight hours, topped with melt-in-your-mouth chashu pork belly and a perfectly marinated egg.
Tokyo-Trained Sushi Chefs: From premium, fresh salmon maki to crispy, golden gyoza, the attention to detail is unmatched.
The Ultimate Comfort Food: Whether you need a cozy date night spot or a comforting bowl of spicy Hell Ramen after a shopping spree, the atmosphere is vibrant, warm, and highly inviting.
Don't settle for fast-food chains. If you want the most authentic Japanese dining experience in Southampton, head to Westquay today and grab a bowl!

Don't settle for fast-food chains.

If you want luxury Japanese food in Southampton, THIS is the place!

I was lucky enough to dine here the night before they opened to the public, the menu is extensive and well thought out, it covers all options from Meat/Fish to Vegan/Halal.

We tried multiple shrimp and prawn starters, like the amazing dynamite prawns 🦐. And the beef ramen paired with multiple sushi platters all of which is good value for money while maintaining an upscale feel to the restaurant.

Not to mention the cocktails which are just remarkable!! (Pictures attached) And taste absolutely incredible.

Overall, caters to all different preferences and the staff are really friendly.

Massive shout out to Willow and Liana who served us sat in the back corner, your food/cocktail recommendations and friendly banter made the night really memorable for us, we'll be coming back!!

Edit: Months later and staff and food are still lovely!!

Update 2 - I've seen the reply. I have zero interest in eating somewhere that caused a week of illness. Anecdotally I've heard that this branch isn't as well regarded as others elsewhere me.  I'm leaving this review as a warning to others. Examine your food thoroughly if you do decide to eat here.

reviews.text:
The food here was lovely and the manager (I think as he knew a lot about the dishes and is the most charismatic out of all the staff) made sure we were well taken care off during the entire service. The atmosphere here is such a vibe with all the sticky notes on the walls from past customers enjoying the food and their choice of music (J pop with a lot of Ado) really set the vibe.

Now onto the important stuff, the starters were nice such as the Takoyaki which was crispy albeit a little bit under seasoned and the tempura squid which fell under the same boat. For the mains, I had the steak tataki ramen which was amazing as the broth was nice and aromatic. The beef was cooked rare initially which was nice and juicy and as it simmered in the broth ended being medium which was nice. We did find that the black garlic ramen was a little bit bland though compared to the steak tataki ramen. Overall, a nice Japanese place for foods and vibes!

reviews.author: Brinley Morgan
reviews.text:
Full disclosure, my meal was comped. The food is great, sitting between Wagamama and Hokkaido in terms of quality. Service was impeccable, Willow was incredibly friendly and helpful, absolute pleasure to meet them.
The atmosphere was energetic and loud, based on my one experience I would recommend this for group dining with friends/family. I wouldn't personally pick it as a date spot as I struggle with sensory overload but it would be an option for less sensitive people I'm sure!

The price point was surprisingly good considering the portion sizes and quality of the food, I think if I want to enjoy some nice Japanese food without splurging on Hokkaido this would definitely be my first port of call.

The Seafood Hell Ramen was topped with a generous portion of Seafood which I really wasn't expecting and I'm already craving another, the Miso Soup was great which is always a good sign when a restaurant gets the simple things right. I wasn't sold on the maki biru house beer but the cocktail I had called Geisha's Kiss (A recommendation from Willow) was incredible,  just make sure you pay attention to your waiter and wait for the dry ice to finish reacting before drinking it! Oh and the Hibiki Whisky was a fantastic little cap to the dinner, I'll be sure to try more of their selection.

All in all, fantastic place, will happily go back for the staff and food though I would prefer if the music was a little lower.

reviews.author: Jack Jack
reviews.text:
Absolutely fantastic meal! The chicken broth ramen was full of flavour, with a rich, comforting broth that tasted like it had been simmering for hours, and the noodles were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of bite. Every spoonful was warm, satisfying, and packed with depth. We also ordered the fried chicken side and the fried octopus, and both were cooked perfectly – crispy on the outside, tender inside, and packed with flavour. Everything arrived fresh and hot, and the portions were generous without feeling too heavy.

The restaurant itself was spotless and really well kept, which made the whole experience even better. The atmosphere was great too – relaxed, welcoming, and ideal for a casual meal or a quick stop while shopping. The staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome throughout our visit, which added to the overall experience. It’s clear that a lot of care goes into both the food and the service here. We went off the £18 lunch menu and added some premium options making it an average of £20 a head which is amazing value for money. Huge portions too!

Easily one of the best places to eat at the Metrocentre. We left feeling really impressed and already talking about what we’d order next time. We’ll definitely be back!
complaint_clauses: We went off the £18 lunch menu and added some premium options making it an average of £20 a head which is amazing value for money.

reviews.author: L.G. Obreja
reviews.text:
I had the pleasure of visiting Maki & Ramen in Glasgow today at precisely 14:18, comfortably within their advertised lunch offer window (valid until 15:00). Or so I naively believed.
Instead of being served, I was told I couldn’t order because I “wouldn’t have time to eat before 15:00.” This is a remarkable reinterpretation of basic hospitality—apparently, customers are now expected to justify not just arriving on time, but also their projected eating speed.
What made the experience truly memorable, however, was the staff. The waitress was dismissive and unnecessarily rude from the outset, making it very clear that customer service was not high on the priority list. Any attempt to question the logic of the refusal was met with attitude rather than explanation.
To add a final layer of confidence to the situation, a very young staff member—who introduced himself as the “general manager”—stepped in to reinforce the decision. Whether this was meant to reassure me or simply end the conversation quickly is unclear, but it did little to inspire trust in how the place is run.
So to summarise: an active offer that you can’t actually use, unhelpful staff, and management that seems more improvised than professional. If you’re looking for a restaurant that honours its own terms and treats customers with basic respect, you may want to look elsewhere.

reviews.author: Tegan Young
reviews.text:
Me and my boyfriend went to Maki and Ramen for an early dinner as we wanted to try out the new restaurant in West Quay. There was a small queue (about 5 groups) when we got there with just one person greeting and taking people to their tables. There was also a member of staff dressing the tables near the welcoming area who had noticed the queue but did not come to seat or call someone to seat the queue. Eventually another member of staff came over to seat us. The restaurant was lovely and tidy and the food was incredible. We cannot fault the food at all: we both got the chicken ramen as there was a lot of the options out of stock ar 5pm on Saturday). The lady who served us said her name was Tinky (on the reciept it says we were served by Chuwei X). We were told about the options being out of stock before we could look at the menu, which was appreciated as we then were able to chose another option and not have the disappointment. When we ordered, Tinky did not seem very interested in me and my partner as we did not want any sides/extra drinks/deserts. We ordered a main and a drink and our bill came to nearly £40! After we had asked for the bill, it took about 10mins just for Tinky to get the card reader when we had seen other tables immediately able to pay.

TLDR: food was lovely but if you are just going for a main and a drink, youre better off going elsewhere!

reviews.author: Regan Roberts
reviews.text:
I got SEVERE FOOD POISONING after eating here last Wednesday. This restaurant has been warned by other customers multiple times about serving food at improper temperatures going back 5 months, as several 1-star comments here show. The ramen I got should have been served piping hot as per Japanese tradition. It was just warm enough for me to not bother sending it back. HUGE mistake. I'm now on day four of being sick with diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, and stomach cramps. It is NOT WORTH THE RISK to eat at a restaurant like this that demonstrates such NEGLIGENCE when it comes to protecting the public! Some 180 people every year DIE from food poisoning in the UK alone and this establishment is obviously NOT taking its warnings seriously! I have filed a complaint with the Aberdeen City Council as should anyone else who has been served food at an improper temperature regardless of whether they got sick or not.

Regarding the restaurant's response: I am pleased the health department acted swiftly, but I doubt they arrived at 5:30pm, which was when I was there. Also, as my review was left before their inspection, the restaurant had ample warning and time to prepare for it. The fact remains that multiple guests had already complained of food being served at improper temperatures going back 5 months prior to my visit and as of the date of my visit, that issue had still not been corrected and as a result I was horribly ill for several days. I don't consider that 'holding high standards for food safety.'

reviews.author: Shubby
reviews.text:
This was our first time visiting Maki & Ramen after hearing some good reviews, and overall it was a pleasant experience.

The restaurant is nicely decorated with a welcoming atmosphere, and the staff were friendly and quick to seat us. We weren't overly hungry, so we ordered two dishes: the Hell Ramen and the Rainbow Roll.

The Rainbow Roll was interesting to look at because of how the toppings were assembled. Instead of each piece having the same topping, they were mixed throughout the roll, with some pieces topped with salmon and others with tuna, as shown in the photos. This made it a little difficult to appreciate the individual flavours of each type of maki, but overall it tasted fresh and was enjoyable.

The Hell Ramen was the highlight of the meal and made the visit worthwhile. It had a great level of spice, the broth was rich and full of flavour, and the toppings were fresh, and well presented.

Overall, we left satisfied with our meal. The food was good quality, reasonably priced, and the service was welcoming. We'd happily visit again and would recommend giving it a try.
complaint_clauses: We weren't overly hungry, so we ordered two dishes: the Hell Ramen and the Rainbow Roll.
but overall it tasted fresh and was enjoyable.

reviews.author: Daisy Black
reviews.text:
There’s something quietly magical about finding a place that makes you feel completely at ease, especially when you’re dining alone.

I visited Maki & Ramen as a little solo date with myself, armed with a good book and no plans other than to enjoy the afternoon. From the moment I walked in, Eirini welcomed me with such genuine warmth that any nerves I had about eating alone disappeared instantly. Her kindness and attentiveness struck the perfect balance—always there when needed, while still giving me the space to savour the moment.

The food was incredible, comforting, and beautifully presented, but what I’ll remember most is how the whole experience made me feel. It became one of those unexpectedly special afternoons that reminds you your own company can be enough.

Thank you, Eirini, for making an ordinary lunch feel like such a lovely memory. I’ll be thinking about it for a long time, and I’ll absolutely be back.There’s something quietly magical about finding a place that makes you feel completely at ease, especially when you’re dining alone.

The customer service was terrible.

Organisation and communication definitely aren’t their strong suits and I’m still trying to figure out what they are.
Surprisingly, they cooperated with some free meals after we mentioned we waited over 30 minutes as per the lunch deal policy. That certainly softened the blow.

I love Japanese food and culture, but this was far from it. And you should stay far from it also.

reviews.author: S X
reviews.text:
The staff were friendly and the restaurant was clean, so no complaints there. However, the food was a major disappointment, especially given the prices.

Everything arrived so quickly that it felt less like a restaurant meal and more like pre-prepared food being assembled. The ramen lacked the depth, freshness, and attention to detail I would expect from a place specializing in Japanese cuisine. The broth tasted generic and lacked the richness of a properly cooked stock, while the noodles and toppings felt highly standardized and pre-portioned.

What also struck me was that I couldn't see any real kitchen operation, which only reinforced the impression that much of the food was prepared elsewhere and simply finished on-site.

The biggest surprise, however, was the rating. After eating here, I genuinely struggled to understand how this place scores so highly. Perhaps many customers are drawn to the Japanese branding, trendy atmosphere, or fast service, but based on food quality alone, I found it very ordinary.

reviews.text:
偽寿司屋です。おすすめしません。
美味しくない。日本食で働いておいてアジア人差別をする最低な店員がいます。
I went to this restaurant with my Asian friends. I visited because the website menu showed an “omakase aburi sushi” option, which I was interested in trying. However, when we arrived, it was not available on the actual menu.

I asked a male staff member about it, and he told me that if we requested it, the chef could prepare an omakase with some aburi (seared) sushi. When the female server came over, I explained that we would like to order omakase with aburi sushi. She asked which pieces we wanted to be seared, which was reasonable. However, when I asked, “Which sushi pieces would normally be selected?” because it was omakase, she did not check with the chef or try to help. Instead, she replied bluntly, “It’s omakase,” and left it at that.

The restaurant was not busy at all — there were only two other tables occupied — yet this server repeatedly came back almost every minute asking if we had decided what to order. The constant pressure, combined with her unfriendly attitude, made the experience very uncomfortable.

As a Japanese person, I found this level of service especially disappointing from a restaurant that presents itself as serving Japanese cuisine. I believe staff should have a better understanding of Japanese dining culture, especially the meaning of “omakase,” where customers trust the chef’s selection.

The most frustrating part was that when we paid using a certain service, her attitude suddenly changed. She became friendly, smiled, and even asked us to leave a review. So here I am, leaving an honest one.

Unfortunately, the sushi itself was not good, and the sushi was not prepared by a Japanese chef. In my opinion, this felt more like a fake representation of Japanese sushi rather than an authentic sushi experience.

reviews.author: Di sgg
reviews.text: This was my second visit to this restaurant, and unfortunately the experience was even worse than the first. When I arrived, a staff member asked if I had any allergies. I told them that I can’t eat spicy food because I have an allergic reaction and my throat starts to itch. I was assured that this would be taken into account. After we were seated, our order was taken about ten minutes later. I specifically ordered a non-spicy ramen. There was nothing on the menu indicating that the dish was spicy. However, when my food arrived, it was spicy. When I pointed this out, staff initially argued with me. Only after I reminded them that I had told them about my allergy beforehand did they take the dish back. I then had to wait another twenty minutes for a replacement. Mistakes involving food allergies are not just inconvenient, they can be dangerous. I had also ordered a dessert, but after some time I was told that it was no longer available and asked to choose something else. After all that had happened, my appetite was already gone. What makes this even more disappointing is that this was already my second negative experience. During my first visit, I waited around forty minutes for my food because my order had been forgotten. After I left a review, I was told that if I came back, the service would be much better. Unfortunately, this second visit turned out to be even worse. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously, especially when it comes to handling customers with food allergies. These mistakes are not only careless, but can pose a real risk to health. Sadly, after two such experiences, I don’t think I’ll be returning to this restaurant.

reviews.text:
The ramen at Maki & Ramen surprised us all when we dropped by for a quick bite before our day trip.  We ordered the ambitious sounding "black garlic" and the cartoonish sounding "hell" ramens.

Both came out quickly, looking very well put together.  The ramen noodles were unapologetically firm, as they should.  The broth was rich from the taste of bone extracted slowly.  The chashu held the right balance of tender meat and jellied fat.

We were impressed that such bowls were possible in Edinburgh; the best we had in the UK so far, out of 6 places we've tried.

The quality here was easily comparable to the better ramen we get in the Bay Area and would even be acceptable to the locals in Tokyo and Osaka.  The chef or owner clearly knows and cares what she's doing.

reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we didn’t even get the chance to try the food, so I can’t comment on that. However, the customer service was the worst I’ve ever experienced.

From what I saw in the two minutes we were there, it’s a beautiful venue in a great location. We decided to visit after seeing it advertised and my partner purchased a Groupon voucher, as neither of us had been there before.

When we arrived, we immediately told the receptionist that we had a Groupon voucher. She welcomed us, did a big show with a drum showed us to a table, and said everything was fine. A few moments later, another member of staff came over and told us we couldn’t use the Groupon voucher on weekends, that could be totally avoided.

The frustrating part is that this restriction wasn’t made clear on Groupon, and if weekends weren’t eligible, the receptionist should have told us before seating us. Instead, we were seated, which was embarrassing and completely avoidable.

The restaurant looks lovely, and although the menu apparently nice, we were happy to give it a try. Sadly, the poor customer service completely changed our impression.

Losing two customers means losing much more than that. We won’t be returning, and unfortunately we can’t recommend the restaurant to our friends, family, or clients. A simple apology doesn’t make up for being treated so dismissively.

I hope the management takes this feedback on board and invests in better staff training and clearer communication regarding promotional offers. This experience wasn’t just about the Groupon voucher, it was about how we were treated.

treated so dismissively, simple apology doesn't make up

reviews.text:
It may say more about me than anything but dining at this establishment has completely restored my faith in dining out in the UK. The presentation and service were so incredibly refined and high end for the price point, I was left completely impressed. The level of customer service, the sheer politeness and competence displayed by the wonderful staff is something that I genuinely have not experienced in decades. It  made me realise how modernity has reduced my expectations in food culture to the point where a mediocre experience is enough to make me happy. That will no longer be the case as I will return soon and seek other establishments that offer elevated experiences.

I sat down at table 9 and ordered at 17:54. The staff, especially on front of house deserve the highest praise and reward. Thank you for this experience.

The chefs selection option was also great, where the chef selected the freshest cuts and pieces for us. The service was also fantastic with Kayley being clearly very knowledgeable about the menu and attentive, and made the whole experience great. We were also served by Ken who we later learnt was doing a trial shift, who was also lovely. We were also given a free desert and sake to try which we all thoroughly enjoyed. Definitely would recommend to anyone wanting an a special, personalised and great value dinner.

reviews.author: Fion
reviews.text:
​Fantastic Beef Ramen & incredible set lunch deal!

We stopped by before a medical appointment nearby, looking for something special and new to try, and this place truly delivered!

​As Asians who eat a lot of ramen (where tonkotsu or chicken is standard), finding a Beef Ramen with such a rich, authentic beef broth was a very welcome surprise. It was deeply flavorful and delicious!

​What blew us away was the set lunch deal: £18 for a main, side, and drink! Adding just a £2 top-up for the beef ramen (which is normally £17.50  à la carte) made it incredible value for money for our family of three.

​What we ordered:
​2 Lunch Sets: Beef Ramen (rich broth & delicious noodles), crispy Tempura, freshly fried, and crispy Takoyaki.

​Sushi: Tiger Roll (super fresh and flavorful).

​Drinks: Generous tea servings that went perfectly with the meal.

​The service was wonderful too—the staff were warm, welcoming, and attentive. There is a cute big-eyed young man makes the restaurant more Japanese feel. Thanks Jannut, Ren and Joceln.

​Fantastic food, great service, and top-tier value.

reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ (1/5)

Very disappointing experience. We came back because our first visit was good, but the quality has dropped dramatically.

The so-called soft-boiled ramen egg was completely hard-boiled with no runny yolk at all. The pork katsu was badly overcooked and black on the outside, making it dry, unpleasant and impossible to eat. Even more disappointing, the "Japanese " tonkotsu served with the ramen was just small pieces of shredded pork, not proper slices of tonkotsu as you would expect from a Japanese restaurant.

This was nowhere near the standard a restaurant serving Japanese food should offer. The food quality was extremely poor and nothing like our previous visit 9 months ago.

The only positive was that the staff were friendly and helpful. The ramen were remade and they apologized for the batch of fully boiled eggs (yet they still served them to customers) with a slightly discounted price. Unfortunately good service could not make up for the very disappointing food. The chef should genuinely understands and delivers the authenticity of the food they are selling.

Sadly, we won't be returning unless the food quality improves significantly.

reviews.author: Luke Patterson
reviews.text:
My partner and I visited today after seeing lots of positive reviews on social media, and overall we had a really enjoyable experience.

Firstly, every member of staff we spoke to, including the managers, was incredibly friendly and welcoming. The managers came across as genuinely caring and approachable, which made a great first impression.

We did have a couple of small issues with the wrong drinks being brought over and a bit of a wait, but it was completely understandable as our waitress had only just started. She was lovely—friendly, welcoming, and you could tell she genuinely enjoys her job. The manager also resolved everything promptly and professionally, which we really appreciated.

As for the food, it was really good. The meat had a great depth of flavour, and both the octopus balls and prawn tempura were fresh, crispy, and delicious. The drinks were good too, although I’d love to see a few more beers available on tap, as I think there were only two options. One small thing I would mention is that the lemonade was served in a plastic takeaway cup. Personally, when you’re dining in at a restaurant, I think drinks should be served in proper glasses.

The noodles were delicious, and the broth was enjoyable, but I felt it could have had a little more subtlety and depth. It relied quite heavily on seasoning rather than building more layered flavours. That said, it was still very tasty, and I’d happily order it again.

Overall, we had a great experience. The friendly service and welcoming atmosphere really stood out, and we’ll definitely be back.

reviews.author: N A
reviews.text:
Visited and decided we were going to sit outside. All the staff were inside huddled together in a corner chatting and didn't even notice I was standing by the door waiting for someone to hand me a menu and ask whether they accepted cash. It actually took one of the chefs to notice me and tell them there was a customer waiting. I honestly didn't even realise they were the staff because the atmosphere made it seem like they were just a group of friends sitting around laughing and talking together. Very unprofessional.

I was told cash was accepted, but when the same staff member came to take our order, she said that because we were sitting outside we'd have to scan the QR code on the table and pay by card. I reminded her that I'd already said we'd be paying cash, which really should have been explained from the beginning.

She then said she could take our order, but we'd have to pay straight after ordering, which was absolutely fine. However, when she told me the total, it was higher than what I'd worked out from the menu prices. She hadn't mentioned that a service charge had been added, and I had to ask twice before she explained what the extra charge was.

Considering the service we'd already received, I asked for the service charge to be removed. From that point on, her attitude noticeably changed and the customer service became even worse. When we finished eating, I thanked her and got no response at all.

The food itself tasted good, but for the price, the portion sizes were very small and definitely need improving.

Overall, a very disappointing experience. The lack of professionalism, poor communication and unfriendly service completely overshadowed the food. Unfortunately, I won't be returning.

Toilets needed a clean and the floor a mop (rather sticky) and the kitchen floors did not look clean either. Leave you doors open and public will look in. reviews.text:
I went for the first time yesterday and had an incredible time- I'm an electric wheelchair user, and from the moment I went in the staff were incredibly attentive and accomodating.

They seated us in a place where my chair could fit and wouldn't be blocking anyone from getting past, and when they realised the table was a bit low for me, they went and got wooden platters to stack under the table to raise the height. Despite being short-staffed, the whole evening Quinn and Hannah made sure I was comfortable, and when I let them know I have coeliac disease, they came out with a gluten-free menu right away and replaced the soy sauce with a gluten-free version without needing to ask.

I had the salmon avocado sushi, and it was so good- you could smell the mirin when it came out, and the fish was so fresh. Definitely the best salmon sushi roll I've had.

Despite my friend and I staying until closing time, the staff were super kind and Quinn checked some of the gluten-free dessert options for me since I'd forgotten to check the menu earlier.

The staff with the black hair and beard was also very helpful, and made sure the table was fixed when he realised it had started to wobble.

Incredible first experience here, and I'd be delighted to come back again. My only complaint was that the music was a little loud, but nothing unbearable. Thank you!! ♡

The food was great but unfortunately the overall experience was disappointing.

We ordered the lunch deal yet we were still overcharged. When checking the bill we were told that the drinks we chose were “premium drinks” with a £2 surcharge each and therefore not included in the lunch deal. Even though the staff member who served us had clearly confirmed that those drinks were not listed as premium on the lunch deal menu.

As we were in a rush to leave she offered to remove the service charge, but somehow we still ended up paying the extra drink charges anyway (not sure what’s happened here..)

On top of that, we tried to order the chicken karaage and the bone broth ramen but were told that neither was available… which was surprising for a ramen restaurant.

Also, when we asked for takeaway containers we were given paper bowls and told that the soup would likely spill if we used them..?

reviews.text:
Absolutely loved this new ramen spot! Everything we ordered was delicious.

The Steak Tataki was a great starter, the Three Kinds Sashimi was incredibly fresh with generous, thick slices, and the Seafood Hell Ramen had a rich broth with a proper spicy kick.

The sides were just as impressive. The Dynamic Prawn with its refreshing yuzu flavour was amazing, and the Pumpkin Croquettes were crispy on the outside and soft inside. The cocktails were also excellent—it’s exactly the kind of place where you can enjoy both great food and drinks.

A special thank you to Navin for the fantastic service. Everyone on the team was warm, attentive and welcoming. We’ll definitely be back!

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 10/10 – Outstanding Experience at Maki Ramen Old Street!
I left Maki Ramen on Old Street completely full, so satisfied, and so thoroughly impressed by the incredible flavours!
As a solo diner, going out alone can sometimes feel intimidating, but the team here made me feel so comfortable, welcomed, and confident from the moment I walked in. I honestly wouldn't have had such a fantastic dining experience if it weren't for them.
A huge, heartfelt thank you to the whole team:
Hajora for the warm welcome and setting such a wonderful vibe right away.
Navin for making sure everything was running seamlessly.
Maria for her attentive care and fantastic energy.
Amidu for the efficient and friendly service throughout the meal.
Jannat for going the extra mile with those thoughtful touches that make a huge difference.
If you’re looking for rich, comforting, flavour-packed ramen and top-tier hospitality—especially if you're dining solo—Maki Ramen Old Street is an absolute must-visit. I'll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Alexis NF
reviews.text:
On two outstanding occasions we visited Maki & Ramen, and we were nowhere near prepared to enjoy the most gracious and giving experience even before we got to food! I don’t remember the last time I felt as thrilled as I did before coming to Westquay. This entire experience completely reinvented what sitting for dinner should feel like, and I’m so grateful that my family were able to really enjoy some special moments with food that just met the mark!

Mia served us service with a smile, a chat, a laugh - a welcome we’ve never had the pleasure of having upon being seated in such a pleasant restaurant. She took the time to give us the best recommendation according to our tastes, drinks to pair perfectly which cut through the savouriness of our meals and really brought out the best in our dishes. Describing Mia’s efforts as amazing to make sure we were satisfied would be an injustice, as everything from the start to finish totalled to what was genuinely the perfect brunch.

The food itself was just as astonishing and excellent as the service! We went all out and ordered, our eyes were feasting as much as we were. Particularly loved my spicy chicken teriyaki and rice meal and the karaage!!
Can’t recommend Maki & Ramen enough! Thank you to the whole team! ❤️
complaint_clauses: Mia served us service with a smile, a chat, a laugh - a welcome we’ve never had the pleasure of having upon being seated in such a pleasant restaurant.

reviews.author: Rosana Anunciacao
reviews.text:
I genuinely don't understand how this restaurant has such a high rating.

We walked past it a few days earlier and decided to give it a try because it had great reviews and looked like a really nice place. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge disappointment.

The service was embarrassingly poor and completely below the standard the restaurant claims to offer. The place itself looked dirty and gave the impression of very poor hygiene.

The most shocking part was the sushi. It was absolutely awful—worse than cheap supermarket sushi. It certainly didn't taste fresh and definitely didn't seem like it had been made that day. The only decent thing we had was the fried chicken, which was actually quite good. Sadly, that wasn't enough to make up for the rest of the experience.

After leaving my review, I did a quick Google search and discovered that the restaurant only opened on 10 April 2026. What I found even more surprising was that it already had over 400 reviews, the vast majority of them positive. Given the quality of our experience, I genuinely struggle to understand how that is possible. While I can't say why this is the case, the numbers simply don't seem to add up from my perspective.

Overall, it was a complete disappointment from beginning to end, and I certainly wouldn't recommend it.

Although the ramen and food were lovely, the customer service was disappointing, especially from the manager.

I’ve visited several times with colleagues and friends, hoping each visit would be better, but unfortunately we have left disappointed every time. The staff were not accommodating to customers’ needs, and the overall service lacked warmth and professionalism.

What made the experience even more frustrating was that a service charge was already included in the bill, even though it is optional. This puts customers in an awkward position and makes the dining experience uncomfortable. A service charge should reflect good service, not be assumed.

The food is genuinely good, but the consistently poor customer service means I cannot recommend this place until it improves.

reviews.author: Afterlife Addict
reviews.text:
I gave Maki & Ramen a second chance, and I instantly regretted it.

The food wasn’t even the biggest issue. The customer service, especially from the manager, completely ruined the experience. Instead of listening to our concerns or trying to find a solution, the manager was defensive throughout the conversation. We weren’t expecting anything unreasonable, just some understanding and a willingness to resolve the situation.

To make matters worse, we were still charged a mandatory service charge, despite receiving service that was far below expectations. It’s disappointing to be expected to pay extra for an experience that left us feeling ignored.

What made this even more frustrating was that we had guests visiting from overseas, and this ended up ruining what should have been an enjoyable evening.

Unfortunately, after giving this restaurant another chance, I won’t be returning. If you’re looking for ramen in Glasgow, I’d recommend trying Ramen Dayo instead. The difference in customer service and overall experience is night and day.

reviews.author: Gavin Jenkins
reviews.text:
Overall, this was a fantastic experience. First impressions were very good, the decor looked beautiful.

Upon entering from the waiting podium we were greeted by an authentic looking (and sounding) taiko drum, which was beaten by a stick by the host leading us to a table. This was followed with all the staff shouting "Irasshaimase!" which is welcome in Japanese. So already you feel pretty good about the experience.

Once seated, the staff were very friendly. We were offered free tap water before we ordered anything.
There were plenty of choices but I went with the black garlic tonkotsu ramen, my partner the vegetarian tonkotsu (which can be vegan also), along with a portion of vegetable gyoza.
All of these tasted amazing and more importantly, authentic. Plus the portion size was more than enough to fill you up.
I did not have any of the sushi but from what I saw being served, it looked very fresh and tasty.

I would recommend this place to anyone who wishes to try out authentic Japanese.

Thank you again to the staff!

We had the rich, deeply flavorful Garlic Tonkotsu ramen, alongside a side prawn and Squid showcased great ingredients and meticulous presentation. Every dish arrived at the table hot, perfectly timed, and crafted with obvious care. Host
was exceptionally knowledgeable, patient, and accommodating, ensuring that every detail of our order was served perfectly.

Highly recommended for anyone seeking both incredible Japanese cuisine and a welcoming atmosphere.

Drinks were genuinely some of the best I’ve had! Best mocktail I’ve had anywhere! I ordered the volcano, sweet but not too sweet and very refreshing. House beer is also a must! The watermelon prebiotic soda might be my new favourite soft drink. TOO many good choices!!!

We had the house beer, Makibiru, with our dinner and stayed for some cocktails afterwards, which were also super delicious! The restaurant itself is decorated so cool, with a really fun atmosphere, and all of the staff seemed genuinely welcoming and lovely.

We were served by Mahak, who was super sweet and absolutely wonderful throughout our visit. She was really patient and helpful with our allergies and dietary requirements, and was attentive throughout the whole evening to make sure we had a great time.

reviews.author: Lime
reviews.text:
Sadly, my experience at Maki & Ramen wasn't the best.

I asked for a Tantan ramen without chili oil, and the waiter said he could ask the chef to use less chili oil than usual. I agreed, but what I got was probably the spiciest dish I have ever eaten in my entire life. Not only was there a huge amount of spicy oil, but there were also plenty of chili pepper pieces!

The eggs were also simply boiled and not like the classic ramen eggs you would expect.

My cousin ordered a Chicken Laksa. The menu described it as *"A Malaysian-inspired twist packed with lemongrass, galangal and garlic. Creamy coconut rounds out this fragrant, warming chicken broth for a bold, exotic experience."* However, there was no chicken in it at all! And of course she paid it the normal price.

After leaving half of our ramen in our bowls, we tried several times to get the waiters' attention to explain what had happened. They either pretended not to see us or said, "One minute and I'll come to you," but then never came back.

After 16 minutes of waiting, we were fed up and simply asked for the bill — and, surprisingly, we didn't have to wait for that.

We will not be returning. We felt completely let down and, frankly, robbed, as we didn't receive what we ordered.

reviews.summary: No-chili request ignored, laksa served without chicken, plain eggs, staff ignored complaint

reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we left feeling quite disappointed with our experience at Maki and ramen, particularly as we had chosen to come here to celebrate our anniversary and were looking forward to it.

We were seated in what felt like a tucked-away corner and unfortunately seemed to be forgotten about. It took around 25 minutes for anyone to come over and serve us, despite approximately 5  members of staff walking past us during that time.

Unfortunately, the service didn’t improve after that. It then took a further 30 minutes for us to receive our drinks, and we had to remind the staff twice that we had actually ordered them even getting our food before our drinks...

We completely understand that restaurants can get busy, especially as this is new to west Quay but it was difficult to understand how our table could be overlooked for so long when there were so many staff members walking passed us.

To make matters worse, when we eventually asked for the bill, we felt like we were suddenly being hovered over by staff, which made the experience feel even more uncomfortable. It was a very different level of attention compared with when we were waiting to be served.

We had been looking forward to having a nice day together. Unfortunately, feeling like we had been shoved into a corner and forgotten about for such a significant part of the meal really put a dampener on what was supposed to be a special occasion.

Hopefully this was just an off day, but based on our experience, the service really needs some attention. We expected a much more attentive and welcoming experience, especially when celebrating something special.

I wouldn’t rush back here.
