This place was ok. The menus could have done with a wipe down. They were sticky. They are also big and bulky, especially the drinks menu.
We were a table of 5 and wished to sit outside due to the lovely weather. The host was unsure as "the tables can't be moved" and made up for 2 or 4. We suggested to split and sit as a 2 and 3, not ideal as we are 2 adults and 3 children. We ended up with a chair at the end of our table but it blocked access to the table next to us.

It was suggested we use the QR to order or pay upfront with the server. We opted to order via the QR, however you you can't order the kids bento on there. So we ended up doing that with the server. All a big fluff to be honest. Sorry we removed the pre added service charge when ordering because why pay service upfront? The staff were nice but this cost them a tip, as we didn't have cash to leave one.

The deco' is lovely but could have done without the faux blossom flowers on the outside as they block the view of the lake.

reviews.text:
The food here is an absolute revelation, every dish was fresh, full of flavor, and prepared with the utmost care. The chefs definitely know what they are doing, and the culinary experience was top-notch. The service in the dining room was also efficient and friendly.

Unfortunately, a big minus goes to the venue's policy regarding the service charge. It was automatically added to the bill upfront, and what's worse, no one informed us about it or asked if we agreed to it. Furthermore, the staff also failed to inform us that this fee could be opted out of entirely.

I would have left a tip anyway because the food and the work of the waiters were worth it, but imposing a service fee in this manner is simply in bad taste and ruins a good impression. It's a shame that such a minor yet unfair practice hurts the image of the entire place. Despite everything, it's worth coming here just for the taste, but the staff should be more transparent with their customers.

reviews.text:
Took my husband to Nottingham’s ‘Maki & Ramen’ for a birthday treat, it’s not really my first choice for food but thought I’d give it a go as it was about him on this day (09.08.26).
Decor is lovely with a big ceiling dragon and cherry blossom, I like that they bang a gong whenever diners are taken to a seat. However the table isn’t very exciting, just plain black chopsticks and soy sauce. I loved all the post-it notes…
I’ve been out for ramen three times in my life, unfortunately I didn’t really like my dish here, I had the steak ramen, steak itself was quite chewy, I enjoyed the half an egg and a few noodles but gave my husband the rest. He had a chicken and noodles dish which looked lovely and I wish I’d ordered that. This review is based on personal taste, I just don’t think ramen is for me.
The two other places I’ve had ramen and did actually enjoy those meals and finished them were at The William Wygston in Wigston (a Wetherspoons so very basic) and by a long stretch Uzamaki in London was the best.
Service here is very efficient and I would recommend to those who enjoy this kinda food. Husband thoroughly enjoyed both his meals!

We approached the server who was kind enough to tell us noodles and broths can be swapped to be as accommodating as possible. She assured us that our server will take us through the menu and help assure we are taken care of.

If that would have happened I wouldnt be writing this.

First of all, we was sat down and not a single server attended us for about 15 minutes, we was confused as we was handed a wallet at the start and all dishes apart from nagiri was containing gluten, when someone finally arrived to take orders, we had to explain our confusion and also explain that the wallet said nothing was gluten free, she explained that the vegitarian dish is the only gluten free dish... coeliacs arent rabbits!

Now this wouldnt have been a big deal but we waited for 15 minutes to have someone "help us" 15 minutes of waiting to hear they dont accommodate and have no dishes other then raw fish and a veggie ramin. Avoid here if you have an allergy!

reviews.text:
We had a bit of a strange experience here. The app charged me for sushi that I’d removed from my basket, which I didn’t realise until after I’d paid. I mentioned it to the waiter, who seemed just as baffled, so I ended up keeping the sushi anyway. Unfortunately, it was some of the worst sushi I’ve had.

The app also automatically adds a tip, which you have to manually remove from your total. I find that quite odd? why am I being asked to tip before I’ve even had my food or received any service? Why am I being asked to tip at all for a QR code?

The ramen broth was definitely the highlight of the meal, but overall, the rest was pretty disappointing especially as we were celebrating a birthday. Hopefully some improvements to the app and food quality are made, as there’s potential here.

We were seating next to a fan after saying how hot it was.
We ordered drinks and the steak ramen, and some panko sushi.
Our food arrived before our drinks and the wait staff came over with drinks apologising for the delay in them. 2 minutes later, they came back and told us they had taken the drinks off our bill due to the wait!! We did not complain or ask for compensation so this was a lovely accomodation.

The food was delicious and very flavourful. Especially as the sushi is prepared fresh at the counter.
We both said we would be dreaming about the food tonight!

Looking forward to enjoying something else from their menu soon. Hopefully, they open some other branches in different locations :)

reviews.author: Zen Cheung
reviews.text: It is usually difficult to eat high-quality ramen in the UK. If you want it, you have to drive all the way to get a chance to eat good ramen. But you never expected that this chain of Japanese ramen shops that are all around you would be such a surprise! I heard from a friend last time that I ate their ramen and thought the soup base was good, so we all tried it this time. I can't believe we were overjoyed. Their steak ramen is very good and the soup base is well-done and rich in flavor. The pork bone char siu ramen is definitely up to par. Maybe it's because the founder is from Hong Kong and went to Japan to study. So the overall quality is more Asian, and the taste is not spoiled due to localization. I give it a thumbs up. All in all, it's worth a try. I'll come back here next time when I'm craving for Japanese ramen.

reviews.author: Theo Chan
reviews.text:
Had a really good experience at Maki & Ramen in Meadowhall. The food was really good, everything tasted fresh, and the staff were very friendly and helpful.

We ordered the black garlic ramen and the hell ramen, and the flavour was really good. My only comment would be that I felt they could have been a little more generous with the soup, as I would have preferred a bit more broth.

We also ordered the Black Dragon Roll. The flavours were great, but the sauce was a little too thin, so the rice absorbed it quite quickly and became a bit soggy. It’s only a small point, but a slightly thicker sauce would make it even better.

There was also a small mix-up with one of the sushi rolls we ordered. However, as soon as we mentioned it, the staff spoke to the kitchen without hesitation and had the correct one remade for us. They even let us keep the original roll, which was a really nice gesture and showed great customer service.

The only minor downside was that it could sometimes be difficult to find a member of staff when sitting in the lower-level seating area, as there wasn't always someone nearby.

One other thing to note is that the lower-level seating area is accessed by a few stairs rather than a slope. It's only around 3–4 steps, so it’s not a major issue, but people with wheelchairs or strollers might find it a little difficult to access that area.

Overall, it was a great experience with good food and excellent service. There are a few small things that could be improved, but I'd definitely come back again.

reviews.author: Farial
reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience at Maki & Ramen Meadowhall.

We visited as a family with our very young daughter. Because she would not eat the food from the restaurant, we had brought a small amount of fried chicken for her.

A member of staff told us she could not eat it because of allergy/cross-contamination concerns. If that is the restaurant's policy, we would have been happy to respect it if it had simply been explained politely.

The problem was the way we were spoken to.

The staff member became extremely condescending and started lecturing us, even making a sarcastic comparison along the lines of bringing food for our toddler being like "going to a shoe shop with shoes."

There was absolutely no need to speak to customers like that.

The whole interaction made us feel singled out, embarrassed and unwelcome. We left genuinely questioning why we were treated in such a hostile manner.

Restaurant policies are understandable. Rude and disrespectful treatment of customers, especially a family with a very young child, is not.

I have raised the matter directly with Maki & Ramen management and hope they investigate it properly.

issues.evidence: became extremely condescending and started lecturing us

reviews.summary: Staff lectured family condescendingly over outside-food policy

reviews.author: Kieran Gandhi
reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience

Absolutely disgusting experience at Maki & Ramen in Southampton today. I have never experienced such poor service, especially when dining with children.

My wife’s food and one of my sons’ meals arrived within a couple of minutes of ordering. Meanwhile, my food and all of our side dishes didn’t arrive until around 29 minutes after we ordered. By that point, my wife and one of my children had already finished eating.

But the worst part was what happened with my two-year-old son.

We specifically ordered a katsu chicken main without the sauce, so he could simply have the chicken and rice. We were told this could instead be ordered as two side dishes. Fine — we agreed. Yet when everyone else’s food eventually arrived, his food had not even been started.

We waited a few more minutes before having to call someone over and ask where his food was. The server checked, and I could clearly see the cook looking through old tickets. It was obvious that the order had simply never been started.

We were then offered his meal for free, but were told we would have to wait for it to actually be cooked. What exactly were we supposed to do? Wait another 20–30 minutes while my food went cold? My son is two years old. This is completely unacceptable.

I asked for further compensation given the situation, and instead of showing any understanding, we were challenged repeatedly about it.

At that point, I was so disgusted and frustrated that I didn’t even eat my own meal. It was taken away, and I left the restaurant having paid for a lunch where I effectively didn’t get to eat.

What makes this even more frustrating is that I noticed other tables around us receiving their food together and being served normally.

I am honestly left wondering whether people who look like me are treated differently in this restaurant. I sincerely hope that isn’t the case, but after today’s experience, I cannot ignore how it felt.

This was supposed to be a family lunch, only a week before my birthday, and instead it turned into an incredibly disappointing and upsetting experience.

The way my two-year-old was treated was particularly disgusting. There was no urgency, no proper explanation and very little empathy.

We will never be coming back to Maki & Ramen. I would strongly encourage the management to look seriously at what happened here, because this is simply not acceptable customer service.

instead of showing any understanding, we were challenged repeatedly

reviews.author: Nicholas Srai
reviews.text:
Dropping from 5 Stars to 1 Star due to shocking management service.

I originally left a 5-star review after an incredible dinner, but returning Saturday evening almost before close completely ruined this venue for me.

We stopped by just to give a friend a quick glance inside for a future visit. The doors were open and people were still eating, but the female manager was at the front host desk looking visibly frustrated while sorting something out.

When I asked if we could show our friend around, she was extremely rude and hostile. When I clarified we didn't want a table, she shut us down with an awful attitude. The male host actually tried to intervene and say it was fine, but her hostility made us walk away completely disgusted.

What makes this so disappointing is that on launch night, this exact same manager was boasting about how welcoming she is and how she treats all her staff "like her own children." The contrast between that fake charm and her actual demeanor was shocking.

To top it off, chairs had already been stacked on tables all across the dining room while paying customers were still eating, making the place look messy and making guests feel rushed.

Great food means nothing if management treats returning customers with total disrespect. I won't be back or recommending this place again.

chairs stacked on tables while paying customers still eating

reviews.summary: Manager hostile to returning guests; chairs stacked during service

reviews.author: Khia Kimi
reviews.text:
I was invited to an exclusive pre-opening evening of food and drinks at this new Japanese restaurant on New Street on Thursday 20th August, and what a fantastic experience it was!

I have to admit, I’m not usually a huge fan of Oriental food, particularly because of the oils often used in cooking, so I wasn’t quite sure what to expect. However, I was pleasantly surprised. The food was absolutely delicious, beautifully presented and the portions were very generous. Everything we tried was full of flavour, and I genuinely enjoyed it.

The drinks were amazing too and complemented the food perfectly.

A special mention has to go to Inka, who was a fantastic host, and to the wonderful waiting team, Norah, Juju and Felicia, who went above and beyond throughout the evening. Their warmth, attentiveness and hospitality really made the experience memorable.

One small note from our return visit: We popped back to show a friend the restaurant and its beautiful interior. We only intended to show them the décor from the doorway, but unfortunately the experience was very different. The manager, Nicky, came across as quite sharp and snappy, and her approach felt unnecessarily hostile. It was disappointing after such a warm and welcoming first experience.

Overall, I’d still highly recommend this restaurant for the food, drinks and the excellent hospitality we received from the team on opening night. I just hope our second experience was an off day rather than a reflection of the customer service going forward.

After being seated, we waited for around 10 minutes without anyone coming to take our order, and eventually had to stop a member of staff ourselves. There was also no QR code on the table for ordering.

The food arrived quickly once we had ordered. The chicken pieces were very salty, and both my friend and I ordered the steak ramen.

Unfortunately, both of us developed diarrhoea later that afternoon. We had not eaten anything else after our meal here, so naturally this was quite concerning. While I cannot say with certainty what caused it, the fact that we both experienced the same symptoms after eating the same meal was worrying.

Overall, the combination of inattentive service, overly salty food and our experience afterwards made this a very disappointing visit.

Btw, 12.5% service charge included.

Very disappointing experience at Maki & Ramen Meadowhall on Saturday 15 August, shortly after 6:30 pm.

We visited as a family with our very young daughter and had brought a small amount of fried chicken for her because she would not eat the restaurant food.

A staff member told us outside food was not allowed due to allergy/cross-contamination concerns. We would have completely respected the policy if it had simply been explained politely.

Instead, the staff member was rude and condescending, continued lecturing us, and made a sarcastic comparison that bringing food for our toddler was like “going to a shoe shop with shoes.”

The way we were treated made us feel singled out and uncomfortable, and honestly ruined the whole meal for us. After that interaction, we could not relax or enjoy the food at all.

The behaviour also left us wondering whether we were being treated differently from other customers.

Restaurant policies are understandable, but customers should still be treated with basic respect.

I emailed Maki & Ramen management about this on 20 August and have not received a response yet.

Five Stars – An Incredible Opening Day Experience at Maki & Ramen!
We had the privilege of dining at Maki & Ramen in Birmingham on their opening day, August 21st, and they knocked it out of the park from day one. The atmosphere was breathtaking, and the prices were exceptionally reasonable for the high quality of the food.

Exceptional Team & Service: A huge shoutout to our main server, Felicia W., who was absolutely perfect. What made the day even more special was how seamlessly the entire staff worked together—everyone was so warm and welcoming, and they constantly checked in on us to ensure we were having a great time.

The Food Highlights: I started with the Salmon Teriyaki Roll, which was fresh and perfectly balanced, followed by a deeply rich bowl of Black Garlic Tonkotsu ramen. My daughter ordered the Chicken Gyoza, a comforting Miso Soup, and the Chicken Katsu Curry, which was crispy, savoury, and cooked to perfection.

We were so impressed that my daughter chose to come back just three days later to celebrate her birthday! Once again, the team delivered another flawless, unforgettable experience for her special day.

Whether you're planning an intimate dinner or celebrating a special occasion, this place is an absolute gem. If you are in Birmingham, Maki & Ramen is an absolute must-visit. We can't wait to come back!

The entrance is like a hallway from a horror video game. There is no one at the upper(street level) entrance at the reception.
You walk down into what looks like it can be the beginning of the murder mystery.
Once you get downstairs alive, you are greeted quickly by the staff which were nice.
During the entire time we were there the ladies restroom had a paper on the door with a very “professional” hand written note: “Cleaning in progress” - at a restaurant this should not be out of order for longer than 15 min maximum.
However it did not seem the have anyone cleaning so I pushed the door to enter because I want to wash my hands before eating, surprisingly there was no one cleaning anywhere. There are 6 toilets - 1st one had the door opened full of cleaning supplies in a very disorganised and dirty way, the 2nd & 3rd toilet were both Out of order with yet another very proper hand write note on them.

Out of the other 3 toiles left - 2 were in an unusable state and only 1 was not completely gross and could be used.

The food was mediocre at best, we were 3 people, we got 3 mains and 1 starter.
They did serve the food very quickly- which makes you wonder a bit, however it was basic at best for some classic dishes.

We paid around 25£ each and we will not return.
I do not and will never recommend a place that does not keep their restroom clean.
Unacceptable for central London!

Highly recommend Maki Ramen!
I visited the Old Street branch for lunch and the staff, food and atmosphere is fantastic.
I had walked past the first restaurant in Edinburgh where I learned about Maki Ramen, the founder's journey, story and philanthropy immediately captured my interest and intrigue.  The menu is clearly geared toward inclusivity, there are halal, vegan, vegetarian options as well as an allergen list provided.
Maki Ramen provides authentic asian dishes that I can actually try (halal) without compromising on taste. Prices are so affordable too!

All the staff were lovely. Our interaction with Navin was particularly memorable. He is kind, friendly and knowledgeable. Me and my family had the most wonderful interaction with him. He genuinely cares about offering excellent service. He also spoke highly of the founder and the team he works with, it's so good to know that workplaces with a healthy and happy work culture exist.

I hear that there are more branches opening in London (i.e Stratford, Westfield) and I look forward to visiting them!

Visited Maki & Ramen on Monday 24/08 and absolutely loved it! 🍜🌸

There was a queue when we arrived, but the staff quickly put tables together for our group of 8 and we were seated within 5–10 minutes. The giant taiko drum when people entered was such a fun touch! 🥁

The decor and atmosphere was beautiful, loved the dark, moody vibe, pink cherry blossom tree and the post it note wall. Great music and lovely vibes overall!

The staff were so friendly and attentive. My sister has a few dietary requirements and they were really careful with her order, making sure her food was prepared separately and checking in with us, which was so thoughtful and reassuring.🩷

We all had the chicken ramen and it was delicious! The broth was so hearty and warming. There’s a great selection of halal ramen, and I love that all the sushi options are halal too, definitely trying those next time!

A special thank you to Hoang (sorry if I’ve spelt your name wrong!) you were an absolute star! ⭐️

Can’t wait to visit again!💕🩷🥢

We ordered the chicken karaage and two ramens (one seafood, one steak). The chicken karaage came out within 60 seconds, something I find very concerning and a red flag in any restaurant. I wouldn’t even believe an excuse of “it sits out cooking ready to go”, because when I bit into my first piece it had red pieces, appearing jelly like and under cooked.

Batter was also very greasy and thick - more batter than chicken. The ramen was pretty average. Egg looked like it had sat out for a long time with a dried out yoke.

The menus and table also didn’t feel very clean. The menu actually felt sticky. Pretty disappointed and certainly won’t be back. Didn’t think it was worth what we paid.

Our server, Elham, provided great service and was very helpful throughout our visit.

As for the food, I really wanted to give 5 stars, but unfortunately there were a few things that let it down. We all had ramen, we ordered the steak tataki, laksa and green curry. The broths were full of flavour and had just the right level of spice for us. I would have preferred the broth to be a little hotter in temperature, though.

Unfortunately, the chicken in both the laksa and green curry was quite bland, as it was served plain without much flavour. The steak tataki was also disappointing as it wasn’t particularly tender and required quite a lot of chewing. It also wasn’t served warm.

Overall, the flavours of the broths were excellent and the service was great, but the bland chicken and tough, lukewarm steak prevented me from giving 5 stars.

reviews.author: Edward
reviews.text:
We’ve been regular customers of Maki Ramen for a while and have also tried their restaurants in both Manchester and London. One thing I really like is how consistent the food is across their locations.

I had the Tonkotsu Ramen, which I’d give around 8/10. It’s not the most authentic or intense tonkotsu I’ve had, but it’s well balanced and definitely suits the local taste. My friend had the Hell Ramen, which I’d probably rate 6/10 — it was okay, but not quite as impressive. The highlight for us was definitely the Chicken Karaage. Crispy, juicy and full of flavour — easily a 9/10.

Overall, Maki Ramen is a reliable choice if you’re craving ramen. We’ve been back several times and the quality has always been pretty consistent.

reviews.author: Chelsea Coley
reviews.text:
My partner and I visited yesterday and honestly, what a find! 🥢🍜
As it was their opening weekend, there were understandably a few items unavailable from the menu, but that didn’t take away from the experience at all. Everything we did try was absolutely fantastic , full of flavour, beautifully presented, and clearly made with a lot of care.
The cocktail deserves a special mention too. Not only was it theatrical and so much fun to watch, but it was genuinely delicious and packed with flavour. 🍸✨ It’s always a bonus when the drinks are just as memorable as the food!
One of our favourite little touches was being given the chance to draw our own pictures on Post-it notes and put them up on the wall. Now we have an excuse to come back and see if we can spot ours on our next visit! 📝😂
There’s something really special about discovering a new place while it’s just getting started, and despite a few teething issues that are completely understandable for an opening weekend, the food, atmosphere and little details already made this place stand out.
We’re not normally gatekeepers… but we might have to keep this one as our little secret. 🤫❤️
Can’t wait to come back, try more from the menu and see how this place grows. Definitely one to watch!

reviews.text:
TL;DR: Highly recommend! Delicious food and most of the menu is Halal. Ask for Navin, best server ever!

What made our experience special was our server Navin. He came and spoke with us as we were settling the bill and honestly, it's been a very long time since I've seen such kindness, authenticity and passion for the role.
Navin took the time to ask us about our experience and spoke about how much he loves his job and how Maki & Ramen is a great place to work, because the owner is a kind and wonderful person who really cares about the staff.
He spoke about how excited he was when the owner asked him to join the new Shoreditch branch and how he's never known a business owner to be so down to earth and kind, someone who he's personally learnt so much from too.
Navin also told us about the charity that the business supports (The Felix Project) and showed us the info leaflet about it. Again, the food is really great but Navin made it a lovely and memorable experience and we hope to see him next time we visit!
